source_prompt:
# Instructions for accurately documenting excessive industrial emissions in an air-quality report

1. Start with the monitoring records.
2.
completion:
Collect all available monitoring records from air-quality sensors, emission control devices, and any supplementary data sources such as manual logs or drone surveillance data within the industrial site. These records should include relevant parameters like particulate matter (PM2.5, PM10), sulfur dioxide (SO2), nitrogen oxides (NOx), carbon monoxide (CO), volatile organic compounds (VOCs), and greenhouse gases (CO2). Indicate precise timestamps and locations to correlate data points accurately.

3. Review industrial permits and regulations.
Understand the specific emissions standards and limits defined in the industrial permits and local, regional, and international regulations. Document these regulations alongside the monitoring data to establish a benchmark for compliance.

4. Conduct visual inspections.
Perform on-site visual inspections to verify that the monitoring equipment is calibrated correctly, in good condition, and that there are no visible sources of excessive emissions (e.g., smokestacks, venting systems). Note any discrepancies observed
